name: Example: Using the Double-Angle Formula Multiple Times
problem: Without using a calculator, find the exact value of $\sin{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{24}\right)}\cos{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{24}\right)}\cos{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{12}\right)}.$
worked_solution:
First, let's recall the double-angle formula for sine: 

$$
2\sin{x}\cos{x} = \sin{2x}
$$

Substituting $x=\dfrac{\pi}{24}$ into the above, we get

$$
2\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{24}\right)\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{24}\right) = \sin\left(2\cdot \dfrac{\pi}{24}\right)
$$

which simplifies as

$$
2\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{24}\right)\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{24}\right) = \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{12}\right) .
$$

Now, we can rewrite the given expression using the above, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{24})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{24})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12}) & =\frac{1}{2}[2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{24})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{24})]\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the double-angle formula once more with $x=\dfrac{\pi}{12},$ we can further simplify the above expression: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12}) & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}[2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{12})] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\sin{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{24}\right)}\cos{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{24}\right)}\cos{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{12}\right)} = \dfrac{1}{8}.
$$
